explanation: Forking is a GitHub platform feature, not a core Git command.
tip: You have full admin rights over your fork.

explanation: Fork = GitHub to GitHub copy. Clone = GitHub to local machine copy.
tip: Typical workflow: Fork on GitHub → Clone your fork locally.

explanation: `upstream` points to the source of truth.
tip: Remember: Origin = My fork, Upstream = The original repo.

explanation: `git remote add upstream <url>` takes 5 seconds and makes future syncing effortless.
Downloads commits from the original repo so you can inspect or merge them.
tip: You can view upstream commits with `git log upstream/main`.

explanation: Forking protects open-source projects from unauthorized or broken code pushes.
tip: Maintainers review all proposed code before it ever touches main.

explanation: Pulls new upstream commits and fast-forwards your local main.
tip: Don't forget to push back to your fork: `git push origin main`!

explanation: The 'Sync fork' button on GitHub is super convenient when you don't have terminal access.
tip: Look for 'This branch is behind...' on your repo page.

explanation: Forks are completely decoupled. You can break anything in your fork without fear.
tip: Feel 100% free to experiment in your own fork.

explanation: Keeping your fork's `main` clean makes syncing with upstream effortless.
tip: Always branch off main for every separate pull request.
